title: Seasonal mailing list
prompt: Marketing sends three mailings a year to every customer: spring, summer and autumn. Write `solve(customers)` so it returns one row per customer per mailing, numbered in that order.
rules: Every customer gets exactly three rows: `mailing_no` 1 with `mailing` `spring`, 2 with `summer` and 3 with `autumn`.
Include every customer, even one whose name or city is missing.
`mailing_no` is a whole number. Return `customer_id`, `name`, `mailing_no` and `mailing`.
hints: `F.lit("spring")` is a column holding the same value on every row, and `F.array(...)` can hold several of them.
Exploding an array that is the same on every row repeats each customer once per element.
`F.posexplode` also gives each element's position, from 0, so add 1 for the mailing number.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(customers):
    # Return customer_id, name, mailing_no and mailing: three rows per customer.
    return customers
explanation: Build the same three-element array on every row and explode it: `customers.select("customer_id", "name", F.posexplode(F.array(F.lit("spring"), F.lit("summer"), F.lit("autumn"))).alias("pos", "mailing"))`, then `(F.col("pos") + 1).alias("mailing_no")`. Each customer becomes three rows because the array has three elements, whatever else is missing on the row. Exploding an array of structs such as `F.struct(F.lit(1).alias("mailing_no"), F.lit("spring").alias("mailing"))` and spreading it with `"m.*"` works too. Positions start at 0, which is why the 1 is added.
